blogs.title: 5 things to prepare before bringing your newborn home
blogs.description: A calm, well-prepared home makes those first weeks so much easier — here's a gentle checklist.
blogs.content:
Bringing a newborn home is one of the most beautiful and overwhelming moments of life. To help you transition smoothly, here are 5 key things to prepare:

1. Set up a dedicated nursing and diapering station.
2. Stock up on postpartum recovery essentials for the mother.
3. Prepare a safe sleep space (like a certified crib or bassinet).
4. Sterilize bottles, pump parts, and newborn clothes ahead of time.
5. Keep a list of contact numbers for your pediatrician and lactation advisor.

blogs.title: Caring for a bedridden parent: a family guide
blogs.description: Simple daily routines that keep your loved one comfortable, safe and dignified.
blogs.content:
Caring for a bedridden loved one requires patience, empathy, and proper technique. This guide offers essential routines:

1. Prevent pressure sores (bedsores) by shifting positions every 2 hours.
2. Ensure proper hygiene with gentle sponge baths and skin moisturizing.
3. Pay close attention to hydration and a balanced soft-diet.
4. Perform passive range-of-motion exercises to maintain joint flexibility.
5. Maintain a positive, cheerful atmosphere in their room to support mental health.

blogs.title: Post-surgery recovery at home: what to expect
blogs.description: Wound care, nutrition and mobility — a week-by-week overview for families.
blogs.content:
Recovering from surgery at home can feel challenging, but knowing what to expect makes a significant difference:

1. Week 1 is all about rest and strict pain management as prescribed.
2. Week 2 focuses on gentle mobility and tracking wound healing/infections.
3. Week 3 shifts to building strength through light therapy and nutrition.

Always ensure you have a trained nurse for complex tasks like IV injections, dressing, and catheter management. Amma Seva provides full-scope home nursing for post-surgery recovery.
blogs.author: Nurse Mercy K.
